transcription_notes: Source: Gunda Gunde MS GG-00106, 1 Samuel section, folio f003r ONLY (2087x2453 px full-page photo; dark mount, page margins, marginal foliation '3' and a pasted catalogue sticker 'C3-IV-56' at the foot of col.1 -- none of which is scripture and all ignored). Hand: a careful, fairly regular Ethiopic (Ge'ez) book hand in 3 columns, ~40 lines/col, with red rubrication for incipits, section openings and word/section dividers. LAYOUT/READING ORDER: text runs column 1 -> column 2 -> column 3 (left to right); verified by narrative continuity (the vow of 1:11 runs off the foot of col.1 and continues at the head of col.2; the naming of Samuel ends col.2 and 1:21f continues at the head of col.3). CHAPTER SPAN: 1 Samuel 1 occupies a SINGLE folio -- it begins f003r col.1 line 1 (red incipit 'ወሀሎ ፩ብእሲ ዘእምነ አርማቴም...') and ENDS f003r col.3 at roughly line ~19-20, closed by a double red rubric '✣✣' and a small red chapter marker read as 'ም ፡ ፪' (='ምዕራፍ ፪', Chapter 2). Chapter 2 (Hannah's Song) begins on the very next line of col.3 with the red rubric 'ጸለየት ሐና ወትቤ ጸንዓ ልብየ...' ('Hannah prayed and said: my heart exults/is strengthened...'). NO further folios were opened or needed; only f003r was used. VERSE SEGMENTATION: the manuscript has NO numbered verses; it marks breaks only with red dividers (✣ and a related cross-form rendered here as ✡) and ።-type punctuation, used inconsistently (sometimes between phrases, not only between verses). I segmented into 28 units by narrative sense following the conventional 1 Samuel 1 division; this is an editorial judgement, NOT a manuscript feature -- the rubric dividers do not map 1:1 to these verse boundaries and a reasonable transcriber could segment v.4-7, v.21-24 and v.25-28 somewhat differently. Verse counts/boundaries should be treated as soft. LEGIBILITY / DAMAGE -- IMPORTANT: columns 1 and 2 are in good condition and broadly legible at 4-5x upscale with unsharp masking; most uncertainty there is at the level of single faint fidel vowel-orders, ambiguous proper-name spellings, and the manuscript's non-standard orthography (it freely writes ሰ/ሠ, ኀ/ሐ/ሃ, doubled and reduced forms, enclitics joined to host words), not illegibility. Column 3 has a SERIOUS water/damp stain along its entire right margin: an opaque brown discolouration that has consumed the rightmost ~1-2 words of most lines in the upper two-thirds of col.3 (tapering near the foot, where the chapter actually ends and is readable). Those lost line-ends fall in vv.21-28 and are recorded as ⟦illegible⟧ tokens with marker 'illegible'; I did NOT reconstruct them from a known Bible text. Roughly 20-25% of all tokens carry an 'uncertain' or 'illegible' marker; these are NOT evenly distributed -- they cluster heavily (a) on the col.3 right-edge water damage (vv.21-28) and (b) on proper names and the book's idiosyncratic spelling throughout. SUBJECTIVE READ: columns 1-2 (vv.1-20) are a genuine letter-by-letter read I have reasonable confidence in (modulo orthographic variants and a few faint vowels); columns 3 (vv.21-28) is partial -- the surviving left ~70% of each line is read with moderate confidence but the damaged right ends are simply gone, so those verses are incomplete by design rather than guessed. This is transcription, not reconstruction; gaps are left as gaps. NUMERAL TOKENIZATION RULE (apply identically in every mirrored witness): every Ethiopic numeral glyph (፩ ፪ ፫ ፬ ፭ ፮ ፯ ፰ ፱ ፲ ፳ ፴ ፵ ፶ ፷ ፸ ፹ ፺ ፻ ፼ and any combination) is its own standalone token at its linear reading position and is NEVER glued to surrounding letters; the adjacent letters tokenize as ordinary Ge'ez words in written order (a proclitic such as ወ- that a numeral separates from its host may stand as its own short token). The 'geez' string is left exactly as written (numeral remains visually adjacent to its word there); only the 'tokens' array is the clean separated word/numeral list, and any uncertain[].token_index at or after a split was incremented so it still points at the same glyph. Applied here to v1 (፩ብእሲ -> ፩, ብእሲ), v3 (ወ፪ደቂቁ -> ወ, ፪, ደቂቁ), v5 (፩ክፍለስ -> ፩, ክፍለስ).
